nodes.description: HUWE1 is a dosage-sensitive HECT-domain E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that controls the abundance of substrates governing neural progenitor proliferation, neuronal differentiation, and the cell cycle (including TP53-associated control of the neuronal cell cycle). Disease arises from a perturbation of this ubiquitination activity in either direction: increased HUWE1 gene dosage (from Xp11.22 microduplication with demonstrated HUWE1 upregulation in patient cells) or missense variants that damage HUWE1 catalytic function. Both converge on impaired ubiquitin-dependent proteostasis in the developing brain, producing intellectual disability and the associated syndromic features.
